purpose: Axitinib is used to treat advanced kidney cancer (also called renal cell carcinoma) in adults. It is typically used after at least one other cancer treatment has already been tried. It helps slow or stop the growth and spread of cancer cells.
how_it_works: Cancer tumors need new blood vessels to grow and survive. Axitinib works by blocking special proteins (called VEGF receptors) that tumors use to build those blood vessels. Without a good blood supply, the tumor has a harder time growing and spreading.
common_side_effects: High blood pressure, tiredness or weakness, diarrhea, decreased appetite, nausea, hoarseness or voice changes, hand-foot syndrome (redness, pain, or sores on palms and soles), weight loss, and headache.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious high blood pressure — your doctor will monitor this closely. It may cause bleeding problems, so tell your doctor if you notice unusual bruising or bleeding. It can affect your thyroid, liver, and kidneys, so regular blood tests are important. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can harm an unborn baby. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as it can increase the amount of drug in your body to dangerous levels.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg taken by mouth twice a day, about 12 hours apart, with or without food. Your doctor may adjust your dose up or down depending on how well you tolerate it and how your body responds to treatment. Try to take it at the same times each day.
